source_read: Publisher HTML (nature.com/articles/s41591-021-01336-3), read in my own browser tab (tab-9, opened and closed by me; no other tab touched, nothing downloaded): every running-text paragraph, counted by script within each section; the Table 1 and Table 2 pages; the Fig. 1 (CONSORT) and Fig. 3 figure pages; the reference list; acknowledgements, contributions and competing interests. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03537014 through the API v2 (protocol, participant flow, outcome measures, adverse events) and the record's version history (versions 0, 25, 26, 43, 44, 56 and 57). Supplementary Information and Reporting Summary (PDF) not read. Step 1 (blind extraction) not run this round, per the round brief.

design.note: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial at 15 sites; the can and cannot sentences fit what the trial measured.

key_findings.note: Fig. 1b: 1,331 phone-screened (986 excluded, 797 unlikely to meet criteria), 345 screened, 131 enrolled, 40 excluded after enrolment, 91 randomized, 1 withdrew consent before dosing; mITT 46 and 44; completers 42 and 37; the country split is in Results › Demographics, 1st paragraph; de jure n = 89 in Statistics and reproducibility, 4th paragraph.
Table 1: every value matches. Recomputed the editors' tests: age t = 2.14 (d.f. 88), P = .035; dissociative subtype chi-square P = .055 (shown as .06); earlier CBT chi-square P = .019.
Both within-group intervals as printed exclude their own estimates.
Efficacy, 5th paragraph, including P = 0.1003 for site.
Recomputed an independent-samples t of 3.13 from the printed means and SDs (printed -3.11).
Fig. 3 carries no printed values; its bar heights are consistent with about 61% and 27% losing the diagnosis and 30% and 5% in remission, on 46 and 44.
Results › Safety, 1st paragraph; counts are only in the unread Supplementary Table 3.

Table 2: suicide attempt 1 (2.3) and suicidal ideation with self-hospitalization 1 (2.3), both on placebo; suicidality AESIs 3 (6.5) [2 ideation, 1 self-harm with ideation] vs 5 (11.4); cardiac AESIs 0 vs 1 (2.3); the AESI category the paper calls 'abuse potential' empty in both arms.
The finding uses the source's word, 'not solicited'; other fields of the card say 'not recorded' (see interpretation gap).
Registry adverse-events module: all 17 counts, the two serious events, no deaths and the absence of any euphoria term match; window to the termination visit (about 18 weeks).

key_findings.correction: Dates, primary outcome, masking and the enrolment of 100 are right for the current record, but two statements need the record's history. (1) At registration (version 0, 24 May 2018) the secondary outcomes were BDI-II change and vital signs; the SDS became the registered secondary outcome on 19 July 2019 (version 26), about 8 months into enrolment and before unblinding. (2) The ecstasy-use exclusion (more than 10 uses in 10 years, any in the 6 months before the first session, or a previous MAPS MDMA trial) entered the registry's eligibility text on 28 October 2024 (version 57); the versions current during the trial (0 to 56) list only 'abusing illegal drugs'. The primary outcome is unchanged since registration.
key_findings.note: Checked through the ClinicalTrials.gov version history in my tab.

reporting_issues.note: Results › Efficacy, 3rd paragraph and Discussion, 2nd paragraph.
Recomputed: the completers' pooled SD is 11.55; 10.5/11.55 = 0.91 and 11.9/11.55 = 1.03; the Fig. 2a legend pairs d = 0.91 with n = 89.
Recomputed the completers' comparison: t = 1.95, d.f. 77, P = .055.
Methods › Statistics and reproducibility, 9th paragraph says paired; d.f. 79 = 42 + 39 - 2.

One addition: the 46 and 44 of Fig. 3 are the arms randomized and dosed; 91 were randomized and the registry flow shows 45 starting on placebo, so the editors' 'everyone randomized' should read 'everyone randomized and dosed' (with 45 the placebo figure is 26.7%).

Reference 14 is Nardou et al. (2019, mice, oxytocin-dependent critical period); reference 15 is Mithoefer et al. (2019). Discussion, 10th paragraph (expectation effects) cites 14; Discussion, 4th paragraph (reopening the critical period) cites 15; Methods › Procedures, 5th paragraph (vital signs before the supplemental dose) cites 14.
The article adds a third enrolment figure of its own (see missed).

domains.note: Central web randomization from an independent vendor, stratified by site, after preparation; I recomputed the baseline imbalances quoted.

Placebo stops 7 (2 after SAEs, 2 after other adverse events, 2 COVID-19, 1 consent) against 4 on MDMA; 10 of the 14 extra integration visits were on MDMA; the de facto estimand adds only three off-treatment 18-week values.
On-treatment 18-week values missing for 4 of 46 and 7 of 44; any 18-week value missing for 4 and 4 (Fig. 1b); missing at random assumed; no tipping-point or worst-case analysis in the article.

A literal RoB 2 path with blinded raters would stop at low; high rests on counting the participant, whose report the CAPS-5 scores, as part of the measurement. That is defensible here, because unblinding is documented with the same design in MAPP2 and the article itself names possible expectation effects as a limitation, but the reasoning should say it so that readers see why a blinded-rater outcome is rated high.

Low for the CAPS-5: the primary outcome has not changed since registration. Not for the SDS: it replaced BDI-II and vital signs as the registered secondary outcome on 19 July 2019, during enrolment and before unblinding; for SDS results this domain would be some concerns.

overall.note: High, following the outcome-measurement domain; the reasoning's limits on what the trial can be cited for match the article.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial is right. One wording fix: results_show and cannot_establish say expected effects such as euphoria were '(deliberately) not recorded' as adverse events, but the article says they were intentionally not solicited as adverse events (Methods › Procedures, 1st paragraph); whether spontaneously reported euphoria was recorded is not stated, and the registry's 5% list has no such term. The rest of the claimed field is accurate, including the abstract's 'highly efficacious', the SSRI comparison and the within-group inference.

missed: Registry history: the SDS, called the key secondary end point in the article, was not the registered secondary outcome at registration; BDI-II change and vital signs were, until 19 July 2019 (version 26). The article, which calls BDI-II exploratory, does not mention the change. Claims citing the SDS result should carry this.

The ecstasy-use exclusion appears in the registry only since 28 October 2024 (version 57), after the trial and the FDA decision; during the trial the registry listed 'abusing illegal drugs'. The card's inclusion_exclusion, selection_effects ('allowed up to 10 times in 10 years'), exposure.polysubstance, cannot_establish and key finding 17 should label it as the registry's current text; the protocol (not read) may well have contained it.

The article gives two enrolment figures: full enrolment of 105 when COVID-19 halted in-person visits (Methods › Participants, 2nd paragraph) and 131 enrolled (Results › Demographics, 1st paragraph; Fig. 1b); with the registry's 100 that is three figures for one quantity.

Main, 3rd paragraph cites reference 13 (Hake et al., 2019), whose title reports that MDMA impairs the extinction and reconsolidation of fear memory in rats, for the statement that MDMA enhances fear memory extinction; a second citation problem beside the 14/15 transposition.

The participant who withdrew consent before dosing was on placebo (registry flow 46 vs 45), so neither estimand covers all 91 randomized; trivial for the estimate, but relevant to the 'everyone randomized' wording.

Main, 2nd paragraph cites a 2020 cost-effectiveness analysis of MDMA-assisted psychotherapy co-written by two MAPS staff (reference 11: Marseille, Kahn, Yazar-Klosinski and Doblin, PLoS ONE), which bears on cl_mdma_ptsd_cost and contradicts Halvorsen et al.'s statement that no formal evaluation existed.
